findings.who: A shareholder whose 2024 losses were suspended for lack of basis. The 2025 K-1 shows only income and no box 16 code D distribution, and the filer deducts the carried-forward loss this year.
findings.why_no: The computed gate looks only at this year's K-1 loss or deduction items and code D distributions. A suspended prior-year loss appears nowhere on the 2025 K-1, so the condition is false.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Are claiming a deduction for their share of an aggregate loss from an S corporation (including an aggregate loss not allowed last year because of basis limitations)"
findings.fix: Add to the gate a question per corporation: "Do you have losses or deductions from this corporation that were not allowed in an earlier year because of basis limits (Form 7203 Part III, column (e), of your 2024 form)?" A yes makes Form 7203 required.

findings.who: A shareholder who sold, gifted, or had redeemed some or all of their S corporation stock in 2025. The K-1 shows income only and no code D distribution.
findings.why_no: The gate covers only loss or deduction items and non-dividend distributions. A disposition is neither, so the computed condition is false and basis (lines 1 and 2) is never asked, though the gain or loss on the disposition depends on it.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Disposed of stock in an S corporation (whether or not gain is recognized)"; p. 3, Line 13 tip: "If a portion of your stock is redeemed, sold, or otherwise disposed of during the year, attach two separate forms"
findings.fix: Add to the gate: "In 2025, did you sell, give away, exchange, or have redeemed any shares of this corporation, or did your shares become worthless?" A yes requires Form 7203, or a refusal if the tool cannot prepare dispositions.

findings.who: A shareholder whose loan to the S corporation was partly or fully repaid in 2025, possibly after losses reduced the loan's basis in earlier years. The 2025 K-1 shows income and no distribution.
findings.why_no: The gate counts only loss or deduction items and code D distributions. Loan repayments are neither, so the computed condition is false and the loans question, whose yes would end the interview, is never asked.
findings.line: f7203.loans_if_req (missed refusal; gain on repayment dropped)
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File: "Received a loan repayment from an S corporation"; p. 4, Line 34: "Debt evidenced by a formal note will result in capital gain ... Any open account debt ... will result in ordinary gain"
findings.fix: Add to the gate: "In 2025, did this corporation repay any money you (or your spouse, if the spouse is the shareholder) had lent it?" A yes requires Form 7203 and leads to the loans refusal.

findings.who: A shareholder who advanced money to the corporation on open account, without a note, where the corporation's K-1 does not report the advance in the loan item.
findings.why_no: The question says "Item I of the K-1 shows such loans". A filer who finds that item blank or missing may conclude they have no loans, though open-account advances count.
findings.irs_text: i7203 p. 3, Part II: "You must complete this section if you have personally loaned money to the corporation"; "Loans made to the S corporation that aren't evidenced by a written instrument are referred to as an open account debt"
findings.fix: Change the reference to "The K-1 may show such loans, but count any money you lent even if the K-1 does not show it."
